scenario: Eight relay runners — Falco, Garza, Hines, Iyer, Joris, Kwan, Lund, and Mori — will be assigned to exactly one of three relay teams: the Harriers, the Kestrels, and the Larks. The Harriers have three runners, the Kestrels have three runners, and the Larks have two runners. The assignment must conform to the following conditions:

rules.description: Falco and Garza are not assigned to the same team.
Hines and Kwan are assigned to the same team.
If Iyer is assigned to the Harriers, then Joris is assigned to the Kestrels.
If Lund is assigned to the Larks, then Falco is assigned to the Harriers.
Mori is not assigned to the Larks.
Exactly one of Garza, Iyer, and Joris is assigned to the Harriers.

The Harriers (3 runners) and Larks (2 runners) must be filled from the remaining six runners. Mori cannot be on the Larks (rule 5). The Larks must hold exactly 2 runners from {Falco, Garza, Iyer, Joris, Lund} (since Mori is excluded). Mori must therefore be on the Harriers or the Kestrels. The Kestrels already have Hines, Kwan, and one more — if Mori were that third Kestrel, the Kestrels would be full, and the Harriers and Larks would fill from {Falco, Garza, Iyer, Joris, Lund} (5 runners for 5 spots: 3 Harriers + 2 Larks). Rule 6 requires exactly one of {Garza, Iyer, Joris} on Harriers. With 5 runners and 5 slots, many arrangements are possible, but Mori cannot be on the Larks in any case.
